title: Analytical Tools and Frameworks
coreMove: Make the industry value curve visible, then redesign it by eliminating, reducing, raising, and creating factors as one coherent move.
sourcePressure: Turn the blue-ocean idea into visible tools: strategy canvas, value curve, four actions framework, and ERRC grid for challenging inherited industry factors.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Using the tools as brainstorming worksheets that add features without changing the curve.

sourceAnchors.name: strategy canvas
sourceAnchors.detail: official support defines it as a one-page visual analytic for seeing the current state of play and a possible future value curve
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A strategy canvas earns its keep when the current value curve is so visible that the team can no longer hide sameness behind polished words.

sourceAnchors.name: four actions framework
sourceAnchors.detail: official support frames it around eliminating, reducing, raising, and creating factors the industry takes for granted
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The four actions force the awkward questions: what disappears, what shrinks, what rises, and what appears for the first time.

sourceAnchors.name: ERRC grid
sourceAnchors.detail: official support says the grid turns those questions into action and helps produce a new value curve
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The ERRC grid matters only when the boxes change work, budget, and buyer experience, not when they become decoration.

hook: Do not open with a competitor scoreboard, a war metaphor, or a generic market map.
Do not use A crowded market is not..., The real strategy is..., or What if growth... as reusable shells.
counterintuition: Avoid Most people assume... but actually... and The opposite is true.
Avoid turning every chapter into competition bad, creativity good.
tryThisNow: Avoid Set a timer for 60 seconds and list... as a repeated action.
Avoid generic reflect on your strategy prompts.
examples: Avoid conference-room whiteboard workshops as the default scene.
Avoid repeating mugs, markers, dosing cups, bike helmets, radiators, bus depots, classrooms, narrow kitchens, or generic dashboard scenes.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: boutique hotel value curve versus chain sameness
exampleSpecs.audience: a hotel manager convinced her service already stands apart
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the renovation budget funds more amenities or a different value curve
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she pins guest complaints beside a hand-drawn canvas and sees her curve shadow the chain hotel almost point for point
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The laundry chute rattles while six guest cards slide across a folding table

exampleSpecs.domain: dental lab rush fees and clinic trust
exampleSpecs.audience: a dental lab owner competing with a national chain
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether small clinics keep leaving after unpredictable charges
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he marks rush fees as an irritant on the curve and must decide whether to eliminate them instead of polishing turnaround promises
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 7:25 a.m., Martin circles three rush-fee complaints on pink invoices

exampleSpecs.domain: tutoring center ERRC grid that became an add-on list
exampleSpecs.audience: an education operator with limited staff and anxious parents
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a new program becomes focused or unaffordable
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: her assistant points to the crowded grid and she reconstructs how every box became one more promise instead of a tradeoff
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "We created everything," Sophie hears from the scheduler before the phones open

exampleSpecs.domain: neighborhood grocer factor list for office lunch
exampleSpecs.audience: a small grocer trying to serve office workers at lunch
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the store competes on speed alone or creates lunch-planning value
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a cashier challenges the factor list after watching office workers abandon baskets at the soup counter
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The lunch aisle is quiet except for soup ladles tapping stainless wells
mustAvoid: repeated grocery dinner-bundle beat from chapter 1

exampleSpecs.domain: salon service curve for sensory-sensitive clients
exampleSpecs.audience: a salon owner who has copied luxury cues for years
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether clients avoid appointments because the experience feels intense
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the old curve over-raised music, fragrance, and chatter before he creates quiet-first appointment blocks
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Javier four no-shows to connect the perfume diffuser with the cancellation log

exampleSpecs.domain: hardware store tagline tested against a redesigned curve
exampleSpecs.audience: a store manager surrounded by big-box price pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the redesigned offer is simple enough for buyers to repeat
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she predicts price will be named first, then hears buyers repeat project certainty after the curve changes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Which phrase would a buyer say in the parking lot without seeing the flyer?

skillTargets: read a value curve for strategic sameness
reject add-on lists that do not change the curve

tryThisNowSpec: Draw one crude value curve for your current offer and put a dot beside the factor that mostly copies rivals.
